newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian avg lending rate slides to 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian avg lending rate slides to 10 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate continued to slide on Thursday, ending 60 basis points lower at 10 percent in poor trade on Zagreb's money market.
Dealers put total trade at 16.3 million kuna against a demand of 18.3 million which could not be met in full due to a shortage of money on offer.

Fresh settlements, all call money, accounted for 9.5 million kuna and were granted at a steady 10 percent. One savings bank paid a higher price of 11 percent, pushing the weighted call money rate one basis point up to 10.1 percent.
Insurers renewed one-week funds at a usual 9.0 percent. One bank charged 16 percent for a smaller one-month loan.
The central bank calculated its kuna midrates for Friday firmer at 6.1679 against the dollar and at 3.5673 against the German mark. -- Laura Lui, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
